resources.string: Porog
Porog

Porog manages an isolated work profile: separate encrypted storage, screenshots off, an input-method allowlist, Tor-only networking, and a container-only wipe. The single guarded threshold that joins your ordinary phone and a hardened workspace — one door, one device. It attests the phone, not the workspace — hardened, not anonymous. Design only; unaudited.
Hardened, not anonymous · key-attested device, not a measured-boot workspace · DESIGN ONLY · UNAUDITED
Self-enrolled profile-owner work profile on stock Android — never device-owner, never a new OS, never “Postern OS”.
Attests the phone, not the workspace. Not the Postern Seal and not measured boot. A rooted or kernel-compromised host defeats the whole boundary.
Sideload / F-Droid first; no Play Store claims. “Porog” is a proposed name, pending trademark clearance.
SCAFFOLD · reference-prototype · UNAUDITED · never provisioned on hardware. built ≠ booted, emulator ≠ hardware, self-checked ≠ audited.
Porog
One guarded threshold between your ordinary phone and a hardened work profile — one door, one device.

Creating a Porog adds a second, separately encrypted Android work profile that you own on your own stock, un-rooted phone. Nothing is rooted, no OS is replaced, and no Google binaries are installed by Porog.
Create Porog
Opens Android’s own provisioning consent screen. You confirm the profile-owner privilege there; Porog cannot grant it to itself.
Provisioning status
No work profile requested yet.
Provisioning dispatched — not ready yet

Android accepted the request and is creating the work profile. Enrollment only truly completes inside the new profile (the DPC’s onProfileProvisioningComplete). This screen, on the personal side, cannot and does not confirm the profile is ready.
Cancelled
You backed out of Android’s provisioning screen. No work profile was created.
This device can’t host a Porog
Android reports it cannot create a managed profile here (missing FEATURE_MANAGED_USERS, provisioning disallowed, or a work profile already exists). An honest dead-end — Porog does not fake it.
Provisioning failed
Android returned a non-OK result code. No work profile was created.
